correctness.rationale: For every finite forest, exact Cauchy–Binet incidence minors give Gram determinant equal to the product of component orders. The two hub-connectivity classes exhaust the forests of K_{2,q}, and their exact counts and weights reproduce all intrinsic volumes. The binomial expectation H_k/k tends to 1/2 by the bounded weak law, making J/D asymptotic to k^(3/2)/(2(q-k+1)); endpoint and oscillatory bounded ranks are covered separately. Pure-Python finite checks pass in all tested ranges, including integer Gram determinants, but are not used to infer infinite truth. Uniform-forest counts follow from the same exhaustive partition without determinant weights and give exact odds k(k-1)/(4(q-k+1)), hence their sqrt(q) crossover.

originality.rationale: Joós–Lángi Corollary 1 covers the universal wedge-sum formula and is fully credited. The assessed contribution is the new rank-dependent intrinsic-volume-induced hub connectivity law for K_{2,q}, including its sharp two-thirds crossover; Padrol–Pilaud–Poullot discuss deformation cones, and Dong–Ge count supertrees of prescribed forests. None of the inspected statements asserts the conditional Gram-weighted forest law or its critical asymptotics. The exact finite specialization is a supporting derivation, not a freestanding novelty claim. The comparison to uniform k-edge forests is an explicit control showing the determinant-induced change in critical exponent.

value.rationale: The statistical observable is canonical: its measure is the exact decomposition of Euclidean intrinsic volume V_k, and its hub-connectivity event is a structural graph-geometric question. The sharp q^(2/3) rank scale and continuous connection probability function distinguish two geometrically natural regimes and are not a generic routine application of the universal zonotope wedge-sum formula. Comparison with unweighted forests shows the weighting changes the connectivity threshold exponent from 1/2 to 2/3, making the geometric dependence quantitatively testable.
